## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.  
Fix `finished_at` before merge because it reports a finish time for a process whose only event is a start.

## Changes

The pull request adds a conditional timestamp to the latest-event row for each process and documents the new column in the schema catalog.

## Critical

- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — Stop reporting start times as finish times — Process 20 has only a `started` event, yet the model sets `finished_at` to that event’s timestamp. The source allows only `created`, `started`, and `cleared`, so a completion timestamp requires an explicit decision about which event records completion. — Consumers can read a finish time for a process that has only started. — Fix: Use the event that represents completion, or name the column `started_at` if it is meant to record starts.

## Important

- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — Document when the timestamp is NULL — Process 30 started and later cleared, but its timestamp is `NULL`. The catalog says “NULL means the process has never been started,” while `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` evaluates only the latest event. — Consumers using `NULL` to identify processes that never started will include processes that started and later cleared.

## Suggestions

- models/schema.yml:12 — comments — Describe the timestamp’s source format — A latest `started` event with `occurred_at = '2026-01-01T00:01:00-08:00' retains its offset. The catalog says “Stored in UTC using the source event timestamp,” and `then occurred_at` copies the source text verbatim. — Consumers relying on the documented UTC format can receive timestamps with a nonzero offset.
